## What kind of empirical contribution

LAR v0.1 explicitly invites empirical contributions in two directions (working paper §8):

- **Task-success benchmarks.** Comparing agent task completion across publishing-side architectures: retrofit HTML, schema.org/JSON-LD entity pages, and LAR-style workflow-organised surfaces, on shared agent tasks. Methodological precedent: WebArena (Zhou et al., 2023), Mind2Web (Deng et al., 2023). Adjacent retrieval measurements: Volpini et al. (2026), Kim & Huang (2026). A planned field study (Marinoni Moretto & Antichi, forthcoming 2026) will run this comparison on mid-market Italian e-commerce; independent replications, alternative methodologies, and adjacent-domain benchmarks (nonprofit, publisher, services) are all welcome.
- **Falsifiability evidence.** The working paper names three conditions that would disconfirm the LAR pattern: operator divergence on basic shape, retraction rather than expansion of publishing surfaces over time, or empirical evidence that retrofit retrieval consistently outperforms structured publication for agent task completion. Evidence pointing in any of these directions is welcome — confirming the pattern is the easy outcome; disconfirming it requires this category.

State which kind of contribution you're making.
